title: Motors and generators
target: Distinguish electrical-to-mechanical transfer from mechanical-to-electrical transfer.
criteria: Trace energy through a motor and a generator.
Identify magnetic interactions in rotation or induction.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A falling weight turns a generator that lights an LED. What is the useful conversion in the generator?
options: Creation of energy without an input.
cpa.guide: The rotating generator transfers mechanical energy into electrical energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A battery powers a small motor that turns a drill shaft. What is the motor’s useful conversion?
options: Thermal energy into charge created from nothing.
Mechanical rotation into battery fuel only.
cpa.guide: A motor uses electrical input to produce mechanical motion.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: What produces the turning effect in a simple current-driven motor?
options: A steady field always causes any stationary loop to spin without current.
Magnetic forces on current-carrying parts create torque.
cpa.guide: Forces on appropriate current-carrying conductors create a net torque.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Why can rotating a coil in a magnetic field produce generator voltage?
options: Rotation changes magnetic flux through the coil.
Voltage requires a permanently open magnetic field line.
The magnet supplies unlimited energy without mechanical work.
cpa.guide: Changing flux induces emf; electrical output requires an energy input.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A motor receives 240 J electrically and supplies 180 J of useful mechanical energy. What is efficiency?
cpa.guide: Efficiency = 180/240 × 100 = 75%; 60 J goes to other outputs.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A generator receives 500 J mechanically and delivers 350 J electrically. Which energy account is consistent?
options: 150 J is transferred to thermal and other non-useful outputs.
cpa.guide: Conservation accounts for the difference. Useful efficiency is 70%, not the inverse ratio.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
